issues.title: Deliminator: drop the delim join for SEMI/ANTI subqueries without blocking operators even when the LHS has a selection
issues.hypothesis: q04 (319ms, 4th slowest) runs EXISTS as a RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN (0.30s) + INNER join lineitem x DELIM_SCAN (0.17s) + RIGHT_SEMI join (0.17s) + a dedup HASH_GROUP_BY on the delim side. Deliminator::Optimize (src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp:66) deliberately keeps the deepest join with the DelimGet when HasSelection(delim_join) is true (orders has a date filter). The idea is that the delim set reduces expensive RHS work. For a plain EXISTS/NOT EXISTS whose RHS is only scans, filters and projections, that reduction buys nothing a single hash semi/anti join does not already do. MANUAL REWRITE TEST: q04 written as `orders SEMI JOIN (SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem WHERE l_commitdate<l_receiptdate)` gives the same result in 283/220/210ms hot, against 303/~300ms for the EXISTS form. A q22-style NOT EXISTS (customer with a filter, anti join to orders) went from 89ms to 61/63ms with the same count of 27085.
issues.plan: In Deliminator::Optimize (deliminator.cpp:58-71), compute `keep_deepest = !candidate.joins.empty() && HasSelection(delim_join)` as now, then add an exception. Set keep_deepest = false when (a) delim_join.join_type is JoinType::SEMI or JoinType::ANTI, and (b) the RHS subtree delim_join.children[1] contains no LOGICAL_AGGREGATE_AND_GROUP_BY, LOGICAL_WINDOW, LOGICAL_LIMIT, LOGICAL_ORDER_BY, LOGICAL_TOP_N, LOGICAL_DISTINCT or nested LOGICAL_DELIM_JOIN. Write (b) as a file-local static recursive helper, not a header change. In those cases the delim provides no pruning before a blocking operator. Keep everything else unchanged, so scalar or aggregate subqueries (q02, q17, q20) still keep the deepest join. Validate: EXPLAIN q04 should show a single HASH_JOIN SEMI/RIGHT_SEMI between orders and lineitem with no RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN. Check that the condition is plain equality, or that IS NOT DISTINCT FROM does not block the BF or perfect HT, and whether a join BF/min-max filter reaches the lineitem scan. Compare results for q04, q21 and q22 with the old build. Also try EXISTS with an extra correlated inequality, and NOT EXISTS with NULL keys (check that the IS NOT NULL filter handling at :217-225 stays correct for ANTI). Then bench.
issues.expected_gain: q04 about -25% (300 -> about 215ms), and q22 if its NOT EXISTS has this shape (ANTI test -30%). About -2 to -3% visible geomean. Hidden EXISTS/NOT EXISTS/IN-without-aggregate templates (q21-like, q16 NOT IN maybe) also stand to gain.
issues.generality: Any correlated EXISTS / NOT EXISTS / IN subquery with simple equality correlation and a filtered outer table. This is a very common analytical pattern. Could get slower: cases where the RHS is a multi-join chain, because the preserved inner join with the delim set acted as an early filter for joins higher in the RHS. Join BFs and dynamic filters should mostly cover that, which is why condition (b) excludes blocking operators but allows joins. If a regression shows up, tighten (b) to also forbid joins in the RHS.
issues.risk: Low-medium. It is a one-file optimizer heuristic change that reuses the existing removal path, which is already exercised whenever the LHS has no selection, so correctness risk is small (the main checks are ANTI and NULL semantics). Performance risk is limited to the multi-join-RHS case described above.

output.memory:
## db_evolve planner memory (duckdb)

### Round log (pilot run, SF1 data, old geomean bar)
- E0001/E0002 contains-selectivity 0.04: retired at SF1 (the plan did not change). At SF10 the plan flips, and it was accepted as E0008.
- E0003 estimate-gated perfect hash agg: q13 -24% but q17 +64%. Estimate gating is the wrong mechanism.
- E0004/E0007 lazy-init perfect HT plus an 18-bit extension: retired (q02 +8%). q13's c_custkey range at SF10 is 1.5M (21 bits), out of reach anyway.
- E0006 run-collapse in agg probe: about 10% less agg CPU, no wall gain. The cost is group creation/finalize, not probing.

### New run (SF10 data; bar: some templates faster beyond noise, none slower)
- G1R1: E0008 contains-selectivity ACCEPTED (q09 1211 -> 709ms).
- G1R2: E0009 per-key BF for multi-key joins ACCEPTED (q09 -15 to -19%).
- G2R1: E0010 OR-filter derivation under a root AND ACCEPTED (q19 347 -> 186, q14 faster). Geomean 249.8ms (1.086x). Follow-up: derive from ORs nested deeper than the direct children of the root AND (q07 gained nothing; unclear why).
- G2R2: dispatched the Deliminator SEMI/ANTI change. Evidence: deliminator.cpp:66 keeps the deepest delim-get join when HasSelection(LHS). q04 runs RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN 0.30s + inner 0.17s + semi 0.17s. Manual SEMI JOIN rewrite: 300 -> 210-220ms. NOT EXISTS anti rewrite: 89 -> 62ms. If it fails on perf: check whether IS NOT DISTINCT FROM conditions or CM projections block the BF/perfect HT on the new semi join (the manual rewrite's RIGHT_SEMI had a 37.9M probe, no BF, 0.89s CPU, and was still faster). If a multi-join RHS regresses, tighten the condition to "RHS is only scan/filter/projection".

### Lessons for dispatching
- Keep diffs out of widely included headers. Use file-local statics.
- Ask implementers to EXPLAIN-check before the full bench. Bench noise is +-10-35% per template on single runs; re-run before calling a regression.
- `dbe-tool sql "q; q; q"` prints per-statement ms; the first run is cold (2-3x slower). Use tail to keep output small. Pipes to grep and multi-command shell lines need approval; a single dbe-tool call piped to tail/cut works. EXPLAIN ANALYZE is truncated at about 110 lines, so the bottom of deep plans cannot be seen. Use `cut -c1-90 | tail -75` to see the lower part of narrow plans.
- MANUAL REWRITE TEST = cheap validation of optimizer ideas: hand-add the predicate or rewrite and time it. Do this before filing optimizer issues (it worked for E0010 and for the deliminator idea).
- rules.md: never change default settings.
- Planner estimates after LIKE filters and outer joins are off by 5-1000x.
- VERIFY probe/build sides in the plan before proposing join ideas; plans change after every accepted plan change.

### Codebase facts (verified)
- HASH_JOIN: LEFT child = probe, RIGHT child = build. BFs only reach probe-side scans.
- Join BF: CanUseBloomFilter in physical_hash_join.cpp (multi-key since E0009); a perfect HT disables the BF.
- Perfect hash JOIN (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:66 CanDoPerfectHashJoin): INNER only, 1 condition, range <= 1,048,576. RIGHT/SEMI/ANTI joins never get it (q13 RIGHT join 1.78s, q04 RIGHT_SEMI).
- Compressed materialization (compress_comparison_join.cpp) wraps join keys in __internal_compress_* projections, which blocks join-filter pushdown. TESTED twice with SET disabled_optimizers: no wall gain on q18/q09. Deprioritized.
- Expression rewriter rule order: optimizer.cpp:50-71 (Distributivity, JoinDependentFilter, PredicateFactoring). JoinDependentFilter handles both root OR and root AND (E0010).
- Deliminator (src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp): Optimize:58-91. HasSelection:112. RemoveJoinWithDelimGet:177 handles INNER/SEMI child joins with colref conditions and adds IS NOT NULL filters. RemoveInequalityJoinWithDelimGet:274.
- LIKE: like.cpp LikeMatcher + contains.cpp (already memchr-specialized). The q13 NOT LIKE scan cost is likely FSST decompression.
- Scan filter estimate: relation_statistics_helper.cpp ExtractGetStats (DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY 0.2; contains 0.04).
- Perfect hash agg: plan_aggregate.cpp:127. Radix adaptation: radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424. Agg HT: aggregate_hashtable.cpp.

### SF10 profile (current best, wall ms): q13 741, q18 651, q09 577, q04 319, q05 260, q03 247, q08 221, q17 218, q07 189, q16 188, q19 180, q22 173, q14 151, q02 80.
- q13: orders scan NOT LIKE 2.72s CPU; RIGHT join (15M probe, 1.5M build) 1.78s; HASH_GROUP_BY 2.50s.
- q09: lineitem scan 3.94s (BF-cut to 3.27M rows); o_orderkey join 1.79s (orders 15M, no dynamic filter).
- q18: subquery agg over 60M lineitem -> 15M groups dominates.
- q04: delim-join EXISTS (see G2R2).

### Directions
- Active: deliminator SEMI/ANTI (q04, q22, hidden EXISTS templates).
- Next candidates: (a) q09 o_orderkey join: orders 15M unfiltered side, so look at a filter or build-side flip. (b) Perfect hash join for RIGHT/SEMI joins (q13 needs a range above 1M). (c) q13/q18 high-cardinality agg (backlog; profile sink vs finalize first). (d) Eager pre-aggregation below the join for q13 (large change). (e) Deeper-nested OR derivation (q07?). Manual-test first.
- Low value: CM blocking pushdown.
- Exhausted: estimate-gated perfect hash agg; agg duplicate-run collapse; LIKE matcher micro-opts.
